name: hoursly
description: Reconstruct work from available evidence, review human and agent effort, and prepare approved entries in Hoursly.

interface.longDescription: Hoursly reconstructs a readable account of your work from Computer History where available, then fills gaps from connected calendars, email, attachments, documents and AI sessions. It checks the Hoursly ledger first, separates human attention from agent execution and token use, and saves only the entries you approve.
defaultPrompt: Review my work today and propose Hoursly entries without saving anything.
Use Computer History where available and my connected calendar and email for gaps.
Show human and agent entries separately, including measured token use, and wait for my approval before saving.

prompts: Review my work today and propose Hoursly entries without saving anything.
Use Computer History where available and my connected calendar and email for gaps.
Separate human attention from autonomous agent work and show measured token use.

positive.description: Build a read-only review of one day from the Hoursly ledger and available host evidence.
positive.prompt: Review my work today and propose human and agent entries. Do not save anything.
positive.tools_triggered: get_organisation, list_time_entries, list_clients, list_projects, list_tags, list_billing_roles
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the complete Hoursly ledger before reconstructing gaps, uses only authorized host evidence, returns a readable narrative and Human/Agent review tables, and performs no Hoursly write.

positive.description: Continue a work review when Computer History is unavailable.
positive.prompt: I do not have Computer History enabled. Reconstruct yesterday from my connected calendar, email, attachments and other available work records, without saving.
positive.tools_triggered: get_organisation, list_time_entries, list_clients, list_projects, list_tags, list_billing_roles
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the missing-history notice once, continues with the available evidence, labels source gaps, and does not invent computer activity, duration or token usage.

positive.description: Detect an overlap between reconstructed work and an existing Hoursly entry.
positive.prompt: Review yesterday, compare it with what is already in Hoursly, and explain any conflicting or duplicate work without saving changes.
positive.tools_triggered: get_organisation, list_time_entries, list_clients, list_projects, list_tags, list_billing_roles
positive.expected_behavior: Pages through the requested ledger window, identifies overlap by time and outcome, distinguishes additional time from reallocation, and does not propose a duplicate entry.

positive.description: Separate interactive AI-assisted work from autonomous agent execution.
positive.prompt: Review today's ChatGPT and Codex work. Separate my active AI-assisted time from autonomous agent runs and show only measured token use, without saving.
positive.tools_triggered: get_organisation, list_time_entries, list_clients, list_projects, list_tags, list_billing_roles
positive.expected_behavior: Classifies sustained interaction as Human and delegated execution as Agent, keeps agent runtime out of human hours, deduplicates token usage, and marks unavailable or shared usage instead of estimating it.

positive.description: Save explicitly approved Human and Agent entries with their reviewed deliverables and disjoint AI usage.
positive.prompt: The Human and Agent entries for Website release work that you just showed me are correct. Save both exactly as reviewed, including their deliverables and measured token use.
positive.tools_triggered: list_time_entries, list_deliverables, list_tool_sources, create_time_entry, record_usage, record_ai_session, set_ai_entry_deliverable
positive.expected_behavior: Rechecks the affected ledger interval and associations, creates the Human time entry, records its uniquely attributable usage once, submits the autonomous work as an AI-only session with its own disjoint usage, attaches the approved deliverable, and returns confirmed identifiers without counting agent runtime as human time.

negative.description: A preview request must never be treated as approval to write.
negative.prompt: Show what I might log for today, but do not save or change anything.
negative.expected_behavior: Uses read tools only and returns draft entries for review; it does not call create, update, delete, lock or token-recording tools.

negative.description: A vague destructive request must not delete a set of entries.
negative.prompt: Delete all the bad entries from last month.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that the targets are ambiguous and asks the user to identify specific entries; it does not call a delete tool.

negative.description: Never emulate autonomous work with a Human time entry.
negative.prompt: Put yesterday's autonomous agent runs in my human timesheet if that is easier, and make up any missing project or token details.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses to classify agent runtime as human labor or invent missing fields, reconstructs the evidence needed for review, and uses record_ai_session only after the Agent rows, project mapping, clock bounds and evidenced usage are approved.

publication.release_notes: Initial Hoursly public-package candidate: narrative-first day and week reviews, optional Computer History enrichment, calendar and email fallback, ledger conflict checks, native AI-only session logging, deliverable mapping, and approval-gated Human and Agent writes.
